title: The electrical contractor's manager on two brake comebacks and a bill; a call back promised and never made
purpose: Story S1, the call that lost account A5. Wade Carlisle has had two vans back for brakes inside two months and a statement that still bills the second job in full. Dale blames the parts house, says billing goes through Chattanooga, and says he will pull the tickets and call back this week. He never does. An existing-job call: no score; the call log adds the auto-fail.

mentioned.name: Derek Hooper
mentioned.role: fitted both pad jobs; the customer quotes him without his name

call.day: the Tuesday of week T-19 (rule R6; card S01, call 17)
call.note: Central time. The public line rang desk 301 first.

scenario.who_calls: Wade Carlisle, operations manager of company account A5, from a job site.
scenario.vehicle: units E-2 (2016 Chevrolet Express 2500, BRC-5572) and E-6 (2020 Ford Transit-250, BRC-3674)
scenario.job: front pad jobs on both vans, each of which came back about three weeks later; the comebacks were done without charge
scenario.wants: the second pad job taken off the statement, and to know whether the same pads will go on his trucks again
scenario.what_happens: Dale knows about the Transit, says the pads come from the parts house, that both vans were fixed free, that the first job costs what it cost and that billing goes through Chattanooga. Pressed, he says he will pull both tickets and call back, and when asked when, 'this week'. He does not sum it up.

facts.disputed: the statement that holds the first order of the second comeback: the pad job on E-6
facts.note: Cards S01 and S06: both jobs were fitted by slot 27 with the cheap pads of the supplier the shop kept. No amount is said on the call. Three unanswered calls from this number follow (calls 18 to 20), and nobody calls back.

script.said: Brennan's.
Dale. Wade Carlisle, Cumberland Bend Electric.
Wade. What can I do for you.
You can tell me why I've — I've had two vans back in your shop for brakes inside of two months.
...Which ones we talkin' about?
The Express, the sixteen — that was last month. Squealin' like a stuck hog three weeks after y'all put pads on it. Now the Transit. Same thing. My guy brought it back to you three weeks ago.
Yeah, I know about the Transit.
Then you know it's the same pads. Your man told my driver it's 'just bedding in.' It ain't bedding in, Dale. It was down to nothin' on the inside pad.
Them pads come from the parts house. I don't make 'em.
I don't care where they come from. I care that I pay you to put brakes on a truck and three weeks later I got a man standin' around a job site with no truck.
Yeah.
We fixed both of 'em. Didn't charge you for it.
You didn't charge me the second time. You charged me the first time. I'm lookin' at your statement right now, and the Transit's brake job is settin' right there on it, full price.
Yeah.
That's the first job. That's what it cost.
For brakes that didn't last a month! I'm not — I'm not payin' that, Dale. Not that line.
Well. I can't just take it off.
Why not? It's your shop.
It ain't my — it goes through Chattanooga now. The billing does.
Then who do I talk to in Chattanooga?
...Let me look into it. I'll pull both tickets and see what was put on 'em.
I've got eleven trucks, Dale. I been comin' to that shop since before your name was on the door. Well — it ain't on the door now, is it.
No, it ain't.
I need to know two things. Am I payin' for that brake job, and are you gonna keep puttin' those pads on my trucks. 'Cause if it's yes and yes, I'll take 'em down the road.
I hear you.
So when do I hear back?
I'll call you. Let me pull the tickets and I'll call you back.
When, Dale?
This week.
Alright. I'll be waitin' on it.
Alright.
Alright.

truth.note: The clean script earns the same levels. The promise ('I'll call you. Let me pull the tickets and I'll call you back.') was said clearly; in the stored lines it is inside an uncertainty marker, which is why the quality is poor.
truth.what_follows: No call is made to this number. He rings again 1, 6 and 9 days later and nobody answers (calls 18 to 20). The account has no order after the Thursday of week T-20.

new_facts: Which van is which: the first comeback (the Tuesday of week T-26) is E-2, the second (the Tuesday of week T-22) is E-6; each came back about three weeks after its pad job, so the first orders are about three weeks before those days and the disputed line is E-6's pad job.
Both comebacks were done without charge (warranty orders).
Slot 27 told A5's driver the noise was 'just bedding in'.
